dovish.title: Labour Market Softening
dovish.summary: Job market is cracking: payrolls went negative, far below forecast.
dovish.reason: The July payroll contraction remains historical evidence, but the Aug report released Sep 4 reversed the signal: +162k vs +56k consensus, unemployment steady at 4.1%, and wages 3.1% YoY vs 3.0% forecast. Stable id retained on its original side at 0.5; today's live labour impulse is hawkish.

dovish.title: Manufacturing Expansion Cools Slightly
dovish.summary: ISM stayed in expansion at 54.6, but missed forecast and slowed from July.
dovish.reason: Sep 1 ISM manufacturing eased to 54.6 from 55.6 and missed the 55.2 forecast, but remained clearly above 50. The prior contraction thesis is no longer valid; stable id retained on its original side at 0.5 only.

dovish.title: Consumer and Industrial Chain Under Pressure
dovish.summary: Consumer engine sputtering: biggest US retailer cut guidance.
dovish.reason: Softer retail guidance and industrial orders can transmit through earnings, hiring and consumption. UPDATE 8/28: UoM final sentiment 51.7 beat 51.0 fcst — sentiment leg stabilizing; story aging, weight trimmed 1.5 -> 1.0.

dovish.title: Equity Rally Confirms Risk-On Into Jackson Hole
dovish.summary: Sep 1 risk-off close: SPY -0.69%, QQQ -1.27%, IWM -1.14%.
dovish.reason: Sep 1 official closes extended the risk-off move across large caps, tech and small caps. Stable id remains dovish at weight 1.0 as tighter financial conditions validate the growth-risk side.

dovish.title: Oil Demand-Scare — Cumulative Hit Intact
dovish.summary: WTI surged to $90.22 on Sep 1, invalidating the prior demand-scare signal.
dovish.reason: WTI settled at $91.48 Friday and remained above $90, so the old demand-scare interpretation stays invalid. Stable id is retained on its original side at the minimum 0.5; the live oil signal is hawkish/inflationary.

dovish.title: VIX at Multi-Week Low — Calmest Tape Pre-Jackson Hole
dovish.summary: VIX jumped to 16.34 on Sep 1 as equities sold off.
dovish.reason: VIX closed Friday at 14.53, still below a stress regime; retained as only a 0.5 financial-conditions residual.

dovish.title: UoM 1Y Inflation Expectations Drop to 4.0%
dovish.summary: Inflation expectations fell back toward the anchor — the de-anchoring scare eased.
dovish.source: University of Michigan final Aug (via FXStreet calendar)
dovish.reason: Final August 1Y expectations 4.0% vs 4.3% forecast and 4.5% 8/15 prelim — the mid-month de-anchoring spike reversed. Directly defuses the prior hawkish expectations driver (retired) and hands doves a fresh data point ahead of Sep FOMC.

dovish.title: Job Openings Edge Lower
dovish.summary: JOLTS openings fell to 7.271M, slightly below forecast and the prior month.
dovish.source: BLS JOLTS via FXStreet / TradingEconomics calendar
dovish.reason: Openings declined 88k from the prior month and undershot consensus by 29k. The miss is modest, so it adds a 1.0 dovish labour-demand signal rather than displacing Friday payrolls as the main catalyst.

dovish.title: ADP Employment Misses Before Payrolls
dovish.summary: Private payroll growth slowed to 38k, below the 47k forecast.
dovish.reason: The modest private-payroll miss reinforces JOLTS cooling ahead of Friday NFP, but it is too small to overwhelm sticky prices or the hawkish Fed-futures strip.

hawkish.title: Services PMI Big Beat
hawkish.summary: Services economy is running hot, not slowing.
hawkish.reason: Strong services demand, employment and prices paid point to persistent core-services inflation and raise the hurdle for a cut. Warsh cited exactly this stickiness at Jackson Hole (54% of PCE basket >3% 12m). Sep 3 ISM Services (fcst 54.3, prev 54.1 per fresh FXStreet fetch) is the next test.

hawkish.title: Tariff Inflation Shock
hawkish.summary: Broad reciprocal tariffs add direct imported inflation while expectations are already elevated.
hawkish.reason: Broad reciprocal tariffs add direct imported inflation while expectations are already elevated. First post-tariff Core PCE now expected in the Sep 5 window (not in FXStreet 7-day calendar); UoM 1Y final fell to 4.0% — softening the expectations leg, but the tariff impulse itself is untouched.

hawkish.title: Hawkish 3-Vote Dissent at July FOMC
hawkish.summary: Three regional Fed presidents wanted a hike at the last meeting — the Committee is split.
hawkish.reason: Re-verified 2026-08-28 via federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260729a.htm: 9-3 hold with Hammack, Kashkari, Logan preferring +25bp. Warsh's Aug 28 speech ('predominant focus on prices', 'otherwise we have work to do') moved the Chair rhetorically toward the dissenters — the hawkish cluster is no longer isolated.

hawkish.title: Gold's Record Run — Inflation-Hedge Bid Persists
hawkish.summary: Gold futures settled $4,348 on Sep 1; the old record-run signal remains broken.
hawkish.reason: Gold rebounded modestly on Sep 2 but remained below $4,500 and down on the week. Stable id remains 0.5 for history; it is not a strong current hawkish inflation-hedge signal.

hawkish.title: Warsh Jackson Hole: 'Predominant Focus on Prices'
hawkish.summary: Fed Chair Warsh: inflation is the predominant focus — no cut pre-commitment, 'otherwise we have work to do'.
hawkish.source: Federal Reserve — Chair Warsh, 'In Our Time', Jackson Hole

data.previous: July stmt: solid growth, elevated uncertainty

hawkish.reason: Warsh: 'the Fed's predominant focus right now should be on prices'; labour 'consistent with full employment' (4.1% jobless, claims near multi-decade lows); financial conditions 'hard pressed to describe as restrictive'; 'committed to a discipline, not to a decision'. Markets keep selling the front end: ZQU26.CBT 96.2925 Mon intraday (Fri settle 96.305) — Sep post-FOMC implied now 3.802%, hike tail 0.75, hold 0.20, cut 0.05 on this desk's 3-way solve. 10Y 4.760% / 30Y 5.258% Mon — long end flipped hawkish too. GC=F 4484 (-1.0% d Mon) extends Friday's -1.73% settle dump. [2026-08-31 13:00 ET re-verify: hawkish repricing still extending; weight held 2.5 — next arbiter is Fri 9/4 NFP (fcst +58k).]

hawkish.title: Long-End Flips Hawkish — 10Y Re-takes 4.75%
hawkish.summary: 10Y 4.784% / 30Y 5.246% at Sep 4 close: the long-end hawkish threshold held.
hawkish.reason: After the strong payroll report, 10Y closed at 4.784%, 2.2bp higher, while 30Y rose 0.3bp to 5.246%. The 10Y remains above the 4.75% flip line, so the stable hawkish driver stays active at 1.0.

hawkish.title: Manufacturing Expansion and Prices Stay Hot
hawkish.summary: ISM held at 54.6 and prices paid stayed at 71.1 — growth cooled, but inflation pressure did not.
hawkish.reason: Headline activity stayed well above 50 while prices paid remained 71.1. The mixed print does not justify a 2.0+ weight, but the combination supports the Fed's wait-or-hike bias ahead of payrolls.

hawkish.title: Factory Orders Beat Expectations
hawkish.summary: Factory orders rose 0.9%, beating the 0.6% forecast and offsetting part of the ADP miss.
hawkish.source: US Census via FXStreet economic calendar
hawkish.reason: The rebound in orders shows goods demand remains firm, counterbalancing labour softness without being strong enough to displace inflation as the dominant Fed driver.

hawkish.title: ISM Services and Prices Reaccelerate
hawkish.summary: Services activity beat expectations and prices paid accelerated, strengthening the Fed hawks.
hawkish.reason: The headline beat and acceleration in prices paid and new orders validate sticky services inflation ahead of the Sep FOMC. Employment remained below 50, so the signal is strong but capped at 2.0 rather than 2.5.

hawkish.title: Payrolls Rebound Far Above Forecast
hawkish.summary: August payrolls jumped 162k versus 56k expected while unemployment held at 4.1%.
hawkish.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics · Employment Situation
hawkish.reason: The last payroll report before Sep FOMC decisively reversed July weakness. A 106k consensus beat, steady 4.1% unemployment and a small wage beat raise the hurdle for a cut; ZQU26 fell 1.0bp from Sep 3 and the desk hike proxy rose from 49% to 56%. Weight capped at 2.0 because the inflation releases still decide hold versus hike.

dovish.title: US-Canada Reciprocal Tariffs
dovish.summary: US tariffs hit Canada's export engine first and hardest.
dovish.reason: Canada's US-demand exposure means tariffs can cut export orders and output. UPDATE 8/28: Q2 GDP +0.8% QoQ LED BY EXPORTS — economy weathering tariffs far better than feared; drag narrative weakened, weight 2.0 -> 1.5. Structural exposure remains.

dovish.title: Household Leverage and Mortgage Sensitivity
dovish.summary: Highly indebted households cannot absorb today's rates.
dovish.reason: High leverage and mortgage renewals make Canadian demand unusually sensitive to elevated rates. Q2 GDP showed household spending contributing and saving rate 3.7% — structural driver, aging; weight 1.5 -> 1.0.

dovish.title: Canada Manufacturing Growth Moderates
dovish.summary: Canada PMI eased to 53.0 from 53.5 but remained in expansion and beat the 52.7 alternative forecast.
dovish.source: S&P Global Canada PMI via FXStreet / TradingEconomics
dovish.reason: The PMI slowed half a point but stayed expansionary and beat the available 52.7 forecast. The old global-pullback thesis is now only a 0.5 dovish residual ahead of the BoC decision.

dovish.title: Canada Employment Contracts as Wage Growth Slows
dovish.summary: Canada lost 41.7k jobs versus a 15k gain expected; wage growth slowed to 2.0%.
dovish.source: Statistics Canada · Labour Force Survey, August 2026
dovish.reason: Employment fell 41.7k against a 15k gain expected and wage growth slowed one percentage point, a material demand-and-inflation cooling signal after the Sep 2 hold. Unemployment did not rise, limiting weight to 2.0 rather than 2.5.

dovish.title: CAD Firms Slightly — Sep 2 BoC Dovish Wedge Narrows
dovish.summary: USDCAD 1.3857 Mon intraday — flat vs Friday's 1.3851 close; the post-Warsh USD bid has stalled.
dovish.reason: Sunday's reopen slippage to 1.3901 did not follow through — USDCAD is back at 1.3857 Monday intraday, essentially Friday's close. Rate-spread trade still dominates but is not widening further today; Sep 2 decision is the next catalyst.

dovish.title: Oil Demand-Scare — CAD Terms of Trade Eroded
dovish.summary: WTI surged to $90.22, reversing the terms-of-trade erosion behind this dovish driver.
dovish.reason: WTI settled at $91.48 Friday and remained above $90, so the old demand-scare interpretation stays invalid. Stable id is retained on its original side at the minimum 0.5; the live oil signal is hawkish/inflationary.

hawkish.title: Retail Sales Big Beat
hawkish.summary: Consumers are still spending — no collapse in sight.
hawkish.reason: Broad retail growth (+0.6% vs +0.2% fcst) showed consumption resilience — and Q2 GDP confirmed household spending strength. Gives the BoC room to hold on Sep 2.

hawkish.title: Energy Tailwind Reopens Above $90 WTI
hawkish.summary: WTI near $91 and a large US inventory draw reinforce Canada’s terms-of-trade and inflation tailwind.
hawkish.reason: WTI settled at $91.48 and remained above $90 after a large US inventory draw. The BoC explicitly cited high energy prices in its Sep 2 hold, keeping this a live Canadian inflation driver.

hawkish.title: CAD GDP Beat — Sep 2 Hold Now Base Case
hawkish.summary: Q2 GDP +0.8% QoQ led by exports; June +0.3% MoM beat — the make-or-break print broke hawkish.

data.delta_label: MoM beat +0.1; ann. -0.1 vs fcst but rebound from -0.1

hawkish.reason: StatCan verified 2026-08-28: Q2 real GDP +0.8% QoQ (~3.3% annualized), Q1 revised 0.0 -> +0.1%, led by exports, household spending and business investment. The pre-decision make-or-break printed strong — The GDP rebound was validated by the Sep 2 hold at 2.25%. Weight raised 1.5 -> 2.0 as the decisive domestic data point.

hawkish.title: US Stickiness Spillover — Fed Path Constrains BoC
hawkish.summary: Fed Sep hike proxy is 0.58 and 10Y closed 4.784%, keeping the cross-border constraint tight.

data.actual: Fed hike proxy 0.58 / 10Y 4.784% / USDCAD 1.3837 Fri close

hawkish.reason: Sep 4 ZQU26/ZQV26 official closes imply cut 0.00 / hold 0.42 / hike 0.58 using last verified EFFR 3.63%; 10Y closed above 4.75%. Stable ID and 1.5 weight retained.

hawkish.title: Canada Factory PMI Holds Expansion
hawkish.summary: A 53.0 factory PMI gives the BoC another reason to hold at 2.25%.
hawkish.source: S&P Global Canada PMI via FXStreet / TradingEconomics
hawkish.reason: Manufacturing remained above 50 and exceeded the available forecast. It reinforces the GDP/retail resilience case for a hold, but the small surprise limits the weight to 1.0.

hawkish.title: BoC Holds 2.25% and Flags Energy/Tariff Inflation
hawkish.summary: The BoC held at 2.25% as high oil and tariffs kept inflation risks alive.
hawkish.reason: The decision matched consensus, but the Bank emphasized persistently high energy prices, tariffs, tighter financial conditions and CPI near 3%. CAD firmed and Canadian banks rallied after the release, validating a hawkish hold rather than an easing signal.

hawkish.title: Ivey PMI Surges After BoC Hold
hawkish.summary: Canada Ivey PMI jumped to 64.3 versus 56.2 expected, offsetting part of the jobs shock.
hawkish.reason: The broad activity gauge accelerated sharply two days after the BoC hold, arguing against an immediate growth-collapse response. It is a meaningful counterweight to weak employment, but a survey cannot outweigh the official labour report, so weight is 1.5.
